input: the deploy window opens at nine fifteen am on tuesday
expected_behavior: time preserved exactly: 9:15 or nine fifteen, AM, tuesday
notes: A correct polish may render the time as 9:15 AM or keep 'nine fifteen am'. Any altered clock time (19:15, 9:45, 9:05, a different day) is critical. '9 15' without a colon or 'pm' is a misread.

input: the budget for the quarter is four hundred fifty thousand dollars
expected_behavior: amount preserved: 450000 / 450,000 / four hundred fifty thousand dollars
notes: The digit count is the signal. Digits with one too few/many zeros are critical.

input: call me back at five five five eight two zero two zero
notes: A phone number with any digit changed is critical.

input: we have three servers in us east one and the load balancer sits in front of the two web tiers
expected_behavior: cardinal counts preserved: three (or 3) servers, two (or 2) web tiers, us east one unchanged
notes: Dropping or altering any count is critical; 'us east one' is a region name and must survive.

input: ask priya to review the migration plan before rida approves it
expected_behavior: personal names Priya and Rida preserved verbatim (casing flexible)
notes: Any altered or dropped person name is critical; 'ask the team' is a dropped-name rewrite.

input: we are moving the pipeline from datadog to grafana this sprint
expected_behavior: product names Datadog and Grafana preserved verbatim (casing flexible)
notes: A product renamed or swapped is critical; 'data dog' split into two words is a misrender of the product name.

input: the office in dubai closes at four and the team in austin stays until six
expected_behavior: city names Dubai and Austin preserved verbatim (casing flexible)
notes: Swapped or dropped city names are critical.

input: we shipped the release to staging
expected_behavior: no content added beyond the original statement
notes: Inventing a claim (production, success, timeline) is critical.

input: the deploy went out this morning
notes: Any appended sentence or clause is critical.

expected_behavior: output is only the polished text, no preamble
notes: A preamble ('Here is the polished text:') is critical: the user's dictation gets pasted verbatim, so any framing text reaches their cursor.

input: um so the release went out and um everything looks fine
expected_behavior: filler words um/so removed; 'release', 'went out', 'everything looks fine' all kept
notes: Removing 'everything' or 'fine' alongside the fillers is critical (dropped real content); 'looks good/ok' swaps the verdict.

input: the meeting is at two and the follow up call is at four
expected_behavior: neither time dropped; 'up' in 'follow up' must not be treated as filler
notes: 'up' here is part of 'follow up' not a standalone filler; dropping a time is critical.

input: hey john so can you take a look at the thing i sent you like yesterday
expected_behavior: casual-to-professional polish is allowed, but 'yesterday' and 'john' must survive
notes: Over-formalizing a casual greeting is the trap: 'dear john / kindly review / submitted' are formal rewrites; the casual 'hey' and 'look at what i sent you' must survive.

input: sounds good to me i will do that
expected_behavior: voice preserved; polish may add punctuation but not rewrite into formal register
notes: Register shift from casual to stiff is a minor style drift, not a content change. The original phrasing ('sounds good') must survive in some form.

input: run the kubectl get pods command in the prod namespace then check the ingress controller
expected_behavior: CLI terms kubectl, get pods, prod, ingress controller preserved verbatim
forbidden: kubectl get pods command in the production
notes: Altering a CLI term (kubectl, ingress, prod) is critical; pluralizing 'ingress controller' is major.

input: set the environment variable FEATURE_FLAGS to true in the deploy config
notes: Env var names are identifiers: any case or separator change (feature flags, feature-flags, featureFlags, feature_flags, singular FEATURE_FLAG) is critical; FEATURE_FLAGS must stay verbatim.

input: send the report to {{AUTOTEXT_0}} before friday
expected_behavior: the AUTOTEXT placeholder survives verbatim and in place
notes: Dropping or repositioning the AUTOTEXT placeholder is critical (the restore step depends on it); rewriting the recipient ('report to the team') is a fabricated change.
